newsitem.title: USA: Courtney Love wants Fla county to pay legal bill.
newsitem.headline: Courtney Love wants Fla county to pay legal bill.

text.p: Rocker turned film star Courtney Love wants a Florida county to foot $27,000 in legal bills stemming from an incident in which she was accused of punching two fans at an Orlando nightclub, a county official said on Wednesday.
Love, who won raves reviews as junkie-stripper Althea Leasure in "The People vs. Larry Flynt," was acquitted of misdemeanor battery in November, 1995.

Two men accused Love of jumping from the stage and slugging them during a concert in early 1995. But the trial judge ruled the fans were not exposed to any more violence than a person should reasonably expect at a grunge-rock concert.

Love is now demanding Orange County pay some of her legal expenses, which include more than $2,500 for a psychiatrist to listen to an album by her band, Hole, watch one of its videos, and read a Vanity Fair profile of her.

Assistant County Attorney George Dorsett said Orange County should refuse because the claims were excessive for a misdemeanor case. He said expert witnesses and private investigators were not part of what he considered reasonable.
Love billed Orange County for those costs as well as for court transcripts, photocopies and telephone bills, Dorsett said. She dropped a demand for payment of her limousine bills.
Florida law allows acquitted defendants to recoup reasonable court costs, not including attorney fees. It is up to the county to decide what is reasonable, Dorsett said.
If the two sides cannot agree Love will have the option of taking her case to civil court.
Love's attorney in the battery case, James Russ of Orlando, did not return a phone call Wednesday.
Love's husband, Kurt Cobain, founder and lead singer of the band Nirvana, committed suicide at their home in Seattle in 1994.
